chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Ima' ibn al-Fudayl said:
I asked him about the polytheists: Do the Muslims initiate combat against them in the sacred month?
He said, 'If the polytheists initiate against them by deeming it permissible (to fight),

then the Muslims see that they will prevail over them in it, and that is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'The sacred month is in return for the sacred month, and for all things, retaliation'.
And the Romans (Byzantines) in this regard are like the polytheists, because they did not know the sanctity or the right of the sacred month.
So they initiate combat in it.
And the polytheists considered it to have a right and sanctity, so they deemed it permissible (to fight) and it was deemed permissible against them.
And the people of rebellion (ahl al-bagh) are initiated against with combat.
ai.seo_question: When do Muslims initiate combat against polytheists during the sacred month?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the juristic principle that the sanctity of the sacred month is relative to the opponent's observance; thus, if polytheists nullify its protection by initiating hostilities, Muslims may reciprocate based on the verse of *qisas* (retaliation). The text further extends this logic to the Romans (Byzantines), who lacked reverence for the month's sanctity, and to *Ahl al-Bagh* (rebels), establishing a consistent framework for initiating combat against those who do not respect the sacred timeframe.
